description: The targetUrl the definition sync sends for each scheduled job (flowcatalyst contract section 4c). The platform has no default target: a job without one fails every firing. Setup per case: settings (flowcatalyst.* keys; unset = default, receivers.path '/fc', receivers.enabled true), handlers (job codes with a registered scheduled-job handler), jobs (code and declared targetUrl; null or blank = none). With subscription-target-base-url set: a job that declares no target and the service has any scheduled-job handler registered and receivers enabled is sent {base without trailing slashes}{receivers.path}/scheduled-jobs; a path target ('/...') is sent {base without trailing slashes}{path}; an absolute target is sent as declared (trimmed). With no base, the declared target is sent as declared, or none. expect.targets is the targetUrl per job in order (null = the field is absent or empty). A case with expect.problem is refused at start-up and the message of a validation problem contains that text: a path target needs the base; any target that is neither an absolute http(s) URL nor a path is refused.
howToRun: For each case configure the settings, register a scheduled-job handler for each code in handlers, declare the jobs, then run the sync (apply) against a fake platform and compare the targetUrl of each job in the scheduled-jobs request with expect.targets (null = absent or empty); for expect.problem assert that start-up/validation fails with a problem containing the text. Regenerate from Java with -Dconformance.update=true (JobTargetsConformanceTest).

cases.name: no target, base, handler: the service's own receiver
a path target resolves against the base, an absolute one is sent as declared
a base with a path keeps it; trailing slashes are dropped
a handler for another job still counts (any handler)
no base: sent as declared, nothing guessed
a path target without a base is refused at start-up

expect.problem: targetUrl '/custom/run' is a path; set flowcatalyst.subscription-target-base-url

cases.name: a non-http target is refused at start-up

expect.problem: targetUrl must be an absolute http(s) URL or a path starting with '/'
